title: Peering DNS UDP-retry race - lab notebook
content:
Context:
- Private deployment customer intermittently sees certificate/name mismatches from our edge when hitting api.customer.internal over peered VPC. Failures ~0.5-2% of requests, spikes during higher traffic.
- Hypothesis evolved: not pure TLS bug on server — look upstream at DNS path. Observed that failures correlate with high-rate DNS activity and some large responses (TXT, long CNAME chains).

Observed symptoms (summary):
- App logs: TLS handshake failures, often: 'SSL: certificate subject name "api.prod.internal" does not match requested host "api.customer.internal"' and 'curl: (35) error:1408F10B:SSL routines:ssl3_get_record:wrong version number' in a few cases.
- Intermittent 502s at app layer when backend selection uses DNS name.
- Metrics: DNS query latency up from 12ms baseline to 120ms during incidents; UDP retries observed.

Timeline & quick repro attempts (local lab, timestamps UTC):
- 2026-03-02 09:14: started capturing with tcpdump on peering interface (peer-eth0) and customer-facing veth.
  tcpdump filter used: 'tcpdump -i peer-eth0 -s 0 -w /tmp/peer.pcap port 53 or port 443'
- 2026-03-02 09:21: first reproducible window: several DNS queries to resolver A (10.0.0.53) returned fragmented/truncated UDP replies (TC=1) followed by quick TCP fallback from resolver. Time between UDP and TCP: ~270ms.
- 2026-03-02 09:23: observed different resolver B answering faster with a cached but stale A record pointing to legacy-edge.internal (causes TLS cert mismatch). Resolver B often responds on first UDP attempt; resolver A sometimes truncated then TCP fallback returns correct record. Race => sometimes app picks early/stale reply.

Commands & raw outputs pulled during session (sanitized):
- dig +dnssec +edns=0 @10.0.0.53 api.customer.internal ANY +time=2 +tries=2
  ;; -> TC flag set; response truncated (flags: qr rd tc)

- dig +tcp @10.0.0.53 api.customer.internal ANY
  ;; TCP response contains full CNAME chain -> final answer points to api.prod.internal (correct)

- tcpdump extract (abridged):
  09:21:12.123456 IP our-priv-peer.56789 > 10.0.0.53.53: 12345+ A? api.customer.internal. (41)
  09:21:12.123789 IP 10.0.0.53.53 > our-priv-peer.56789: 12345 q: A? api.customer.internal. UDP, length 512 (TC set)
  09:21:12.394890 IP our-priv-peer.56789 > 10.0.0.53.53: 12345+ A? api.customer.internal. (41)  # retry over UDP after ~271ms
  09:21:12.395200 IP 10.0.0.53.53 > our-priv-peer.56789: 12345+ TCP  # or resolver does TCP fallback quickly
  09:21:12.395500 IP 10.1.0.42.53 > our-priv-peer.56787: 54321 q: A? api.customer.internal. UDP, length 180  # resolver B response (fast)

- ssl repro (when wrong host chosen):
  openssl s_client -connect legacy-edge.internal:443 -servername api.customer.internal
  CONNECTED(00000003)
  140736...:error:0A00018E:SSL routines:tls_construct_client_hello:no shared cipher
  -----
  certificate: subject=CN=api.prod.internal
  verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
  verify return:1
  depth=0 CN=api.prod.internal

  => indicates server cert is for prod host; mismatch explained by stale DNS answer.

Reproduction steps (clean):
1) Ensure two resolvers in /etc/resolv.conf: 10.0.0.53 (resolver A, authoritative-ish) and 10.1.0.42 (resolver B, caching-forwarder)
2) Run load generator hitting host via name at ~200 qps and capture tcpdump on peer link.
3) Observe occasional early UDP response from B followed by TCP-correct from A.

Hypotheses (ranked):
- H1: UDP truncation + TCP fallback time causes race between resolvers; application or OS uses first response received (from B) even if it's stale, causing wrong backend selection.
- H2: MTU / fragmentation on peering link causes UDP payloads to be dropped/truncated; EDNS0 advertised size too large => truncated responses. Peering VXLAN overhead reduces effective MTU.
- H3: Asymmetric routing: UDP reply takes different path with lower latency (resolver B) resulting in faster-but-stale record.
- H4: Resolver B has poor cache invalidation and returns stale CNAME chain during churn.
- H5: NAT / ephemeral port reuse causing misassociation very unlikely but keep as low-probability check.

Checks performed and notes: 
- sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward/misc looked normal. IPTABLES rules on peering hosts show no DNAT altering port 53.
- Checked MTU: 'ip link show dev peer-eth0' = 1500 on both sides; but underlying tunnel uses VXLAN -> overhead ~50 bytes. Tested ping with 1472 works but large fragmented UDP path likely.
- Re-running dig with +bufsize=1232 reduced TC occurrences. With +bufsize=1232 queries to resolver A rarely set TC.
- tcpdump + iperf tests indicate occasional ICMP 'fragmentation needed but DF set' (firewall drops ICMP sometimes).

Temporary mitigations tried: 
- Forcing DNS TCP on client side for that domain (resolved in app config): reduced incidents to near zero but not ideal.
- Lower EDNS advertised size at recursive resolvers (set to 1232) for this namespace: fewer truncations observed.
- Pinning DNS entries (hardcode) on app side as emergency fallback for critical endpoints — documented in incident runbook.

Proposed long-term fixes / experiments:
- Ask peering team to increase MTU or account for tunnel overhead (e.g., set PMTU properly across VxLAN) and ensure ICMP is not filtered across peering. Owner: Ravi K.
- Configure authoritative resolver to avoid big UDP answers (minimize TXT/CNAME chaining) for customer-critical records, or enable TCP-fast path. Owner: DNS infra team.
- Add explicit DNS TCP fallback policy in our platform resolver or pin a short-term cache to avoid accepting first-come stale replies. Evaluate kernel resolver behavior (glibc) vs systemd-resolved. Owner: me (Maya).
- Consider DNS over TLS/HTTPS for peering links to avoid UDP frag problems; longer term. Owner: platform-security.

Next steps (actionables):
- [ ] Upload full pcap to shared drive and link to ticket INFR-4321 (will do: /tmp/peer.pcap -> Confluence attachments).
- [ ] Ask peering infra to run 'tracepath' between both sides and share ICMP+MTU observations (owner: Ravi).
- [ ] Temporarily set EDNS buffer to 1232 on recursive resolver for this customer and monitor (owner: DNS infra).
- [ ] Add an integration test that simulates truncated UDP + TCP fallback and asserts correct final answer selection (owner: Zoe).

Notes to self / gotchas: 
- Linux resolver acceptance: glibc nss behavior returns the first valid response seen (race). systemd-resolved acts differently; platform containers differ across versions — need to standardize.
- When the early answer points to legacy-edge we may see cascading errors (stale cert) that are indistinguishable from TLS config bugs unless you correlate DNS timeline.
- Keep sample pcap segments small - PCP upload limited in UI.

Quick command checklist to reproduce locally:
- docker run --rm --cap-add=NET_ADMIN byrnedo/alpine-curl sh -c "apk add bind-tools iputils && dig +bufsize=1232 @10.0.0.53 api.customer.internal ANY; dig +tcp @10.0.0.53 api.customer.internal ANY"
- tcpdump -i any -s 0 port 53 -w /tmp/dns-check.pcap
- openssl s_client -connect <selected-ip>:443 -servername api.customer.internal -showcerts

If this spikes again, priority: high (affects failed TLS validation and customer-facing errors). For now, EDNS size tweak + short DNS pinning is lowest-friction mitigation.

----
Misc raw snippets (copied verbatim when helpful):
- curl timing with bad path: 'connect 0.003s, pretransfer 0.012s, starttransfer 0.289s, total 0.292s' (implies DNS decision occurred very early)
- tcpdump note: seen duplicate DNS response IDs coming from different source IPs for same query id — suspicious (may be resolver race + same query id recycling).

If anyone picks this up: check resolver logs (10.0.0.53) for TC flags + EDNS size; check cache policy on 10.1.0.42. Ping me in #private-deploy if you want the pcap.

-- Maya
